entries.partTitle: Modern Data Lakehouse Architecture: S3 Object Storage, Columnar Parquet & Scan Reduction

left.title: Row-Based Format
items: Reads entire rows containing all unused columns.
Saturates storage input output bandwidth during scans.
Higher cloud storage costs for uncompressed data.

right.title: Columnar Parquet
items: Columnar projection reads strictly requested columns.
Snappy compression shrinks storage by seventy-five percent.
Reduces scan volume by ninety percent on analytical queries.

steps.annotation: Monolithic row storage scans all columns regardless of query filters.
Columnar Parquet organizes analytical data into discrete column chunks.
Simulator projects required columns to cut scan volume by ninety percent.
Column projection saves storage bandwidth and reduces analytics spend.

entries.partTitle: AWS Glue Data Catalog & Automated Schema Evolution: Crawlers & Partition Pruning

left.title: Unpartitioned Data
items: Queries scan all files across historical archives.
Slow directory listing degrades query responsiveness.
Multiplies compute query billing significantly.

right.title: Glue Partitioning
items: Hierarchical prefix partitions isolate daily datasets.
Partition pruning skips ninety-one percent of partitions.
Partition indexes accelerate metadata resolution.

steps.annotation: Unpartitioned storage forces query engines to scan full lakehouse volumes.
Glue data catalog maintains partition metadata for targeted query pruning.
Partition engine skips non matching folders to reduce scanned partitions.
Targeted partition pruning slashes analytical execution time and expense.

entries.partTitle: Amazon Athena Serverless Query Engine: Trino Execution, CTAS & Cost Optimization

left.title: Raw CSV Querying
items: Ten terabytes scanned costs fifty dollars per query.
Repetitive dashboard queries generate massive costs.
No compression or columnar optimization applied.

right.title: CTAS Parquet Tier
items: Partitioned compressed Parquet scans under one percent.
Reduces query expense to sixty cents per run.
Ninety-eight percent total query cost savings.

steps.annotation: Querying raw uncompressed files incurs massive per terabyte billing spend.
Serverless Athena queries scan only compressed partitioned columnar blocks.
Optimizer calculates ninety-eight percent savings using structured formats.
Partitioned Parquet optimization delivers sub dollar query executions.

entries.partTitle: Apache Iceberg Open Table Format on AWS: ACID Transactions, Time Travel & Schema Evolution

left.title: Legacy Hive Format
items: Directory based tracking causes write race conditions.
Updates require rewriting entire partition directories.
Lacks historical snapshot isolation and time travel.

right.title: Apache Iceberg
items: Hierarchical metadata tree coordinates atomic snapshots.
Time travel queries inspect historical committed states.
Hidden partitioning isolates users from directory layout.

steps.annotation: Legacy hive tables suffer concurrency corruption and slow listings.
Apache Iceberg provides atomic transaction safety using metadata trees.
Table engine queries historical snapshots using time travel capabilities.
Snapshot isolation guarantees reproducible machine learning audits.

entries.partTitle: S3 Intelligent-Tiering & Enterprise Lifecycle Automation: Storage Economics & Object Lock

left.title: Static S3 Standard
items: Historical cold data sits in high cost standard tier.
Monthly storage bills grow unbounded over time.
Manual tier transitions require complex engineering.

right.title: Intelligent-Tiering
items: Automatically shifts unaccessed objects to cooler tiers.
Zero operational retrieval fees on historical queries.
Seventy percent monthly storage savings on aged data.

steps.annotation: Dormant historical data in standard storage causes runaway expenditure.
Intelligent tiering moves unaccessed objects automatically to cooler tiers.
Simulator proves seventy percent storage savings across aged partitions.
Automated lifecycle tiering reduces costs while preserving instant access.
